failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase. It starts as a note on the nightly card, becomes a draft once its count how often it fires, and is registered when you say yes. Then it is tested on 2000-2023 at a the strict pass mark, and a paper trial runs it on live sessions for 20 sessions. It is admitted only after beating chance and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, with a leak check passing and your yes again. Only then may the allocated paper capital use it, and the final real-money step needs the India gate and your yes. Today no rule has got that far: the stock rules are in the paper trial at 6 to 8 of 20 sessions, with 5 of the 10 winning sessions needed, and the options line is at 5 of 20.

problems.why: It uses internal terms a beginner would not follow, such as "staircase", "India gate", "leak check", "beating chance and the average stock", and "the options line is at 5 of 20", without explaining them.

results.text: How is STT charged on options, and what happens if I let an in-the-money stock option expire?
results.answer: Sir, since 1 April 2026 STT on options is 0.15% of the premium when you sell an option, and nothing is charged on the buy side. If you let an in-the-money stock option expire, it settles by delivery: the call buyer must pay the full value of the shares, and the seller delivers them (a put works the other way round). Both sides pay 0.1% STT on the full contract value, and an exercised bought option adds 0.15% on its intrinsic value. For example, a Rs 980 call with lot 400 settling at Rs 1,020 pays Rs 416 STT, and brokers raise margins from 4 days before expiry and often square off positions that lack the money, so close in-the-money stock options before expiry unless you want the shares.

results.text: Walk me through what you do every day, start to finish, in order.
results.answer: Sir, it starts each evening after the 3:30 pm IST close. The day's prices, flows and your Zerodha snapshot come in, every holding is re-rated and the cut list is written. Then the managed book (the paper copy that acts on the cut list) fills yesterday's plan at today's open, skipping any buy that opened more than 2% above the last close. It marks its positions, checks the 7% stops and writes tomorrow's plan, after which the practice book records the next session's practice picks and the daily call. At night the reconstruction replays the day like a coach, and the nightly exam re-asks the day's questions. At 8:30 am IST the morning view goes out, and between 9:15 and 10:15 the options line decides one index lot. It is all paper; nothing is placed from chat at any step.
